text: Johnson therefore does not found the cause upon his own delight; for the delight of one man may be only the humour of one age, and the bias of one temper. His appeal is to time, and to what time has left of the work. The writer whose credit hangs upon present fashion, upon local customs, or upon the quarrels of a party, may be honoured while the fashion is alive; when it dies, the honour that lived by it dies also. That work alone has made good its claim which still pleases readers separated from the first audience by all their circumstances. Such judges come without favour; they have no friendship for the author, no interest in his opinions, and read him for this reason only, that he yet gives pleasure.
